title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask friends if they're free, suggest a plan, fix where and when to meet, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to Part 2. From here on the course is about the Sindhi you need with friends, around town and at work — the way people really talk in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur and Larkana.

We start with plans. You'll learn **'let's'** (**اچو ته فلم ڏسون** 'let's watch a film', **هلون؟** 'shall we go?'), how to tell friends what to do with short **تون** commands softened by **نه** (**اچ نه!** 'oh, come on!') and warned with **متان** (**متان دير ڪرين!** 'don't you dare be late!'), and how to say you're **about to leave** (**نڪرڻ وارو آهيان**) or **on your way** (**رستي ۾ آهيان**) — even when you haven't left yet.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?
grammar.body:
Sindhi makes suggestions with the **'we' form of the subjunctive** — the present tense without ٿو / ٿا (Unit 17). It ends in **-ون**:

هلڻ → **هلون** halūṃ · ملڻ → **ملون** milūṃ · ڏسڻ → **ڏسون** ɗisūṃ · کائڻ → **کائون** khāūṃ · پيئڻ → **پيئون** pīūṃ · ڪرڻ → **ڪريون** karyūṃ

**1. Shall we …?** — just the -ون form as a question: **هلون؟** 'shall we go?', ڪٿي **ملون؟** 'where shall we meet?'.
**2. Let's …** — **اچو ته** + the -ون form: **اچو ته** فلم **ڏسون** 'let's watch a film'. To one close friend: **اچ ته** …
**3. Why don't we …?** — **ڇو نه** + the -ون form: **ڇو نه** سمنڊ تي **هلون؟**
**4. Going to do something** — oblique infinitive (-ṇa) + **هلون**: چانهه **پيئڻ هلون؟** 'shall we go for tea?', ماني **کائڻ هلون؟** 'shall we go and eat?'.

Ask what the others think with **ڇا خيال آهي؟** 'what do you think?'.

**Trap:** **هلون** is 'let's go'; **هلو** (-و) is an order to *you*: 'go!' And don't use the future (هلنداسين) for a suggestion — it sounds like a decision already made.

grammar.title: Telling friends what to do: اچ نه!, نه وڃ, متان
grammar.body:
You met the imperative in Unit 11. With friends this is how it is really used:

**تون form = the bare stem** — the normal way to talk to one friend, a younger sibling or cousin: **اچ** achu, **هل** halu, **ٻڌ** ɓudhu, **ڪر** karu, **ترس** tarsu, **ٻڌاءِ** ɓudhāi, **ويهه** vehu.
**توهان form = -و** — to a group of friends, or to anyone older: **اچو**، **هلو**، **ٻڌو**، **ترسو**، **ٻڌايو**.
Polite / for later: **-جو** (Unit 18): **اچجو**، **ڪجو**. For one friend the matching 'do it later' form is **-جانءِ**: فون **ڪجانءِ** 'give me a call'.

**Making it friendlier:** add **نه** after the verb to coax: **اچ نه!** 'oh, come on!', **ٻڌاءِ نه!** 'go on, tell me!'. (Before the verb نه means 'don't'.)
**Don't:** **نه** + imperative: **نه وڃ** 'don't go', **نه ڪر**.
**Don't you dare / make sure you don't:** **متان** + subjunctive (verb without ٿو): **متان دير ڪرين!** 'don't be late!', **متان وساري ڇڏين!** 'don't forget!'.

**Trap:** a bare تون command to an elder or a stranger is rude; use **-و** (and جي / سائين). Using **-و** with a close friend is fine — just a bit distant.

examples.native: اچ نه يار، ڏاڍو مزو ايندو!
examples.roman: achu na yār, ɗāḍho mazo endo!
examples.en: Oh come on, man, it'll be loads of fun!

examples.native: ٻڌاءِ نه، اچين ٿو يا نه؟
examples.roman: ɓudhāi na, acheṃ tho yā na?
examples.en: Go on, tell me — are you coming or not?
Call me when you get home. (to a friend)

grammar.title: About to, on the way, running late
grammar.body:
**About to:** oblique infinitive (-ṇa) + **وارو / واري / وارا** + آهي (Unit 17), agreeing with the subject:
مان **نڪرڻ وارو** آهيان 'I'm about to leave' (man) · **نڪرڻ واري** آهيان (woman) · اسين **پهچڻ وارا** آهيون 'we're nearly there'. Add **بس** for 'just about to': **بس** نڪرڻ وارو آهيان.

**Any minute now:** the present tense covers the near future: پنجن منٽن ۾ **ٿو پهچان** 'I'll be there in five minutes'; **اجهو ٿو اچان** 'coming right now'.

**Already set off:** **نڪتو آهيان** (woman **نڪتي آهيان**) 'I've left', **رستي ۾ آهيان** 'I'm on the way'. Not yet: **اڃا نه نڪتو آهيان**.
**Stuck:** ٽريفڪ ۾ **ڦاسي پيو آهيان** 'I'm stuck in traffic' (woman ڦاسي پئي آهيان).

**Running late:** say it about yourself — **ليٽ ٿيندس** (woman ليٽ ٿينديس) — or with the dative and **دير** (f): **مون کي دير ٿيندي** 'I'll be late'.

examples.native: مان گهران نڪتو آهيان، رستي ۾ آهيان.
examples.roman: māṃ gharāṃ nikto āhiyāṃ, raste meṃ āhiyāṃ.
examples.en: I've left home, I'm on my way. (man)

examples.native: شو شروع ٿيڻ وارو آهي، جلدي ڪر!
examples.roman: sho shurūʿ thiyaṇa vāro āhe, jaldī karu!
examples.en: The show is about to start, hurry up!

lines.en: I'm on my way, I'll be there in five minutes!

lines.speaker: Mehak
lines.native: سچي؟ پويان ته ٽي وي جو آواز پيو اچي!
lines.roman: sachī? poyāṃ ta ṭī vī jo āvāzu peyo ache!
lines.en: Really? Because I can hear a TV in the background!

lines.speaker: Sachal

lines.en: Don't stress, but hurry up! We're going for tea — come and find us there.

culture:
Plans in Sindh are made late and loosely, usually in a WhatsApp group, and 'five minutes' is famously stretchy. **رستي ۾ آهيان** 'I'm on my way' is the national white lie — everyone says it, everyone knows. A quick message when you're running late is still appreciated.

A flat 'no' sounds cold. Give a reason (**سڀاڻي امتحان آهي**، **گهر ۾ مهمان آهن**), say **معاف ڪر يار**, and suggest another day: **ڪنهن ٻئي ڏينهن رکون؟** **انشاءالله** can be a sincere 'hopefully' or a polite way of not committing. Many young people, especially women, check with the family first — **گهر وارن کان پڇڻو پوندو** is a perfectly normal answer, not an excuse.

With friends use **تون** and **يار**; with a friend's parents switch straight to **توهان**, **جي** and **سائين / امڙ / چاچا**. Where friends go: in Karachi, **Sea View**, **Do Darya** and Burns Road; in Hyderabad, **Rani Bagh**, the Hyderabad Club area and late-night tea on Auto Bhan Road; near Jamshoro, **Al-Manzar** on the Indus; in Sukkur, the river and **Sadhu Bela**. And the default plan everywhere is the same: **چانهه پيئڻ هلون؟**

tip.title: آهين to a friend, آهيو to an elder
tip.body:
- To a friend: فارغ **آهين**؟ (تون). To an older person or a group: فارغ **آهيو**؟ (توهان).
- Answer: **هائو** (casual) / **جي** (polite) … فارغ **آهيان**.
- **ٽائيم** and **پروگرام** are what people actually say for 'time' and 'plans'.

sentences.native: هائو، ڇهين وڳي کان پوءِ فارغ آهيان.
sentences.roman: hāu, chhahīṃ vaɠe khāṃ poi fāriġu āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Yeah, I'm free after six.
I'm really busy today.

Have you got time? (polite)

sentences.en: No time today, man — shall we meet tomorrow?
Are you busy today? (to an older man)
Yeah, I'm free too.

tip.title: Let's: اچو ته … -ون / هلون؟
tip.body:
- 'Shall we?' = verb + **-ون**: هلون؟ ملون؟ ڏسون؟ کائون؟
- 'Let's' = **اچو ته** + -ون (to one friend **اچ ته**).
- Go and do: verb-ṇa + **هلون**: ماني کائڻ هلون؟
- **هلون** = let's go; **هلو** = go! (an order).

sentences.en: Let's go to the cinema.
Come on, let's go for a walk in the park.
Shall we go out this evening?
Shall we see the nine o'clock show?

sentences.native: ڇو نه ڪنهن نئين جاءِ تي هلون؟
sentences.roman: chho na kanhin naīṃ jāi te halūṃ?
sentences.en: Why don't we go somewhere new?
Shall we go out to eat?

sentences.roman: chhā xiyālu āhe, pārka meṃ milūṃ?
sentences.en: What do you think — meet in the park?
That place is really nice.
The film was great fun.
It'll be loads of fun!

tip.title: Friendly commands: اچ نه! · نه وڃ · متان
tip.body:
- One friend gets the bare stem: **اچ، هل، ترس، ٻڌاءِ**. A group or an elder: **اچو، هلو، ترسو**.
- Coax with **نه** after the verb: **اچ نه!**
- Don't: **نه** before it: **نه وڃ**.
- Don't you dare: **متان** + verb without ٿو: متان دير **ڪرين**!

sentences.native: اچ نه يار، تو کان سواءِ مزو نه ايندو!
sentences.roman: achu na yār, to khāṃ savāi mazo na endo!
sentences.en: Oh come on, man, it won't be fun without you!
Why are you so stressed? (to a man friend)
Don't you forget!

sentences.en: Hang on a sec, I'm coming too.

sentences.en: We'll be there any second, don't worry. (polite)

tip.title: About to, on the way: نڪرڻ وارو آهيان
tip.body:
- About to: verb-ṇa + **وارو / واري / وارا** + آهي: نڪرڻ **وارو** آهيان (m) · نڪرڻ **واري** آهيان (f).
- Already left: **نڪتو آهيان** (f نڪتي). Not yet: **اڃا نه** نڪتو آهيان.
- Very soon: present tense — پنجن منٽن ۾ **ٿو پهچان**.

lessons.title: Running late or can't make it

tip.title: Saying no nicely
tip.body:
- Say sorry: **معاف ڪر يار** (friend) / **معاف ڪجو** (polite).
- Give a reason, often with **انهيءَ ڪري**: گهر ۾ مهمان هئا، انهيءَ ڪري نه آيس.
- Offer another day: **ڪنهن ٻئي ڏينهن رکون؟** / ٻئي هفتي رکون.

new: معاف ڪر يار، اڄ نه اچي سگهندس.

sentences.native: معاف ڪر يار، ليٽ ٿي ويس.
sentences.roman: māf karu yār, leṭu thī viyus.
sentences.en: Sorry, man, I ended up late. (man)
He's always late.
The plan's still on, right?
Yep, it's on. Seven o'clock.

sentences.native: مينهن پيو وسي، انهيءَ ڪري پروگرام ڪينسل آهي.
sentences.roman: mīṃhu peyo vase, inhīa kare progrāmu kainsil āhe.
sentences.en: It's raining, so the plan's off.

tip.title: Who all? ڪير ڪير
tip.body:
- Repeat a question word to ask for a list: **ڪير ڪير** ايندو؟ 'who all is coming?', **ڇا ڇا** وٺون؟ 'what all shall we get?'.
- 'To come and get you' = verb-ṇa + **اچڻ**: توکي **وٺڻ** ايندس.

sentences.en: Who from the gang is coming?
The whole gang is coming.
Shall we have dinner together?

sentences.native: اٺين وڳي تيار رهجو، مان وٺڻ ايندس.
sentences.roman: aṭhīṃ vaɠe tayāru rahijo, māṃ vaṭhaṇa endus.
sentences.en: Be ready at eight, I'll come and pick you up. (man)
Shall we invite Sassui too?

sentences.native: اسين ستين وڳي راڻي باغ وٽ ملنداسين.
sentences.roman: asīṃ satīṃ vaɠe rāṇī bāġa vaṭi milandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We'll meet at Rani Bagh at seven.
Where are we having dinner?

sentences.native: پوءِ مان توکي گهر ڇڏي ايندس.
sentences.roman: poi māṃ tokhe ghara chhaɗī endus.
sentences.en: Then I'll drop you home. (man)
